title: Multiplication Worksheets: Equal Groups and Facts
intro: Multiplication counts equal groups. Connect the factors to a picture, then practise facts with both factors from 2 through 9. The worksheet has room to sketch a strategy instead of guessing a fact.
html:
Four groups of six are more than four plus six

Liam is packing four snack bags for a picnic. Each bag needs six crackers. He writes 4 + 6 = 10 and starts counting out ten crackers, but the bags are not full. The two numbers describe different things: four is the number of bags, and six is the number in each bag.

Each outlined group represents one bag. Count six crackers in each of the four bags.

6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24
4 × 6 = 24

The multiplication sign connects a number of equal groups with the amount in each group. Four groups of six contain twenty-four objects altogether. Adding 4 and 6 combines two numbers once; it does not count six objects four times.

Move from separate groups to an array

Arrange the crackers into four rows with six in every row. The total stays 24. This row-and-column arrangement is called an array. It helps a child see the equal groups and keeps objects from being counted twice.

Turn the array a quarter turn and it shows six rows of four. That is why 4 × 6 and 6 × 4 have the same product. The picnic story still has four bags with six in each; rotating the array changes how we group the objects, not their total.

Use a fact the child already knows

If 4 × 6 is hard to recall, start with 2 × 6 = 12. Two groups of six make twelve, and two more groups of six make another twelve. Doubling twelve gives 24. For 7 × 6, split seven groups into five groups and two groups: 30 + 12 = 42.

If the child says 7 × 6 = 13: ask them to sketch seven groups and place six dots in each. Then ask what their answer is counting. This separates adding the two factor values from counting the total in equal groups.

Build accuracy before rushing

Use a small group of problems at first. Let the child explain a strategy for one uncertain fact, then try that fact again later without the picture. Faster recall is useful, but a time limit is not part of this printable set.

Both factors in these worksheets are whole numbers from 2 to 9, so products range from 4 to 81. This set does not include the zero and one facts or a complete times-table chart. The answer key gives each product in the same order as the questions.
